processing: Mainly steamed as sencha, and tested for matcha in Nagasaki, where its first-flush powder ranked best among early cultivars.
harvest_season: Spring, an early cultivar picked about two days ahead of Yabukita, though Kumamoto's Kuma area found no difference.
appearance_dry: Deep vivid-green needles, helped by high chlorophyll, with a colour one trial compared to kabusecha.
appearance_wet: Vivid green soft leaf, as its high chlorophyll would suggest.
taste_profile: Balanced and mellow with a fresh aroma, relatively low in catechins and high in amino acids compared with Yabukita.
vintage_note: As with other Japanese green teas, it is sold as the current year's spring harvest and best drunk within a year. It is not widely sold under its own name, though it is not hard to find as a single-cultivar sencha.
description:
Sakimidori is an early Miyazaki cultivar known above all for colour. It carries about 1.3 to 1.5 times the chlorophyll of Yabukita, and that shows in a vivid green leaf.

It is mainly made as sencha, but the colour has made it interesting for powdered tea too. A Nagasaki trial rated its first-flush matcha the best of the early cultivars tested, equal to Yabukita and Okumidori.

The cup is balanced, mellow and fresh, with more amino acids and fewer catechins than Yabukita. A minute at 70°C for the first steep is a sensible start.

For growers it is vigorous and productive, though reports on its disease resistance are mixed. Look for it from Kyushu makers, and compare it with Saemidori if you like vivid green teas.
history: The cross was made in Miyazaki in 1979, between ME52, selected from a native Miyazaki plant in 1932, and F1NN27, from a 1953 cross of Yabukita and Shizuoka Zairai 16. It was registered as Norin 47; published dates differ between 1996 and 1997. Later work in Kumamoto and Nagasaki looked at yields, matcha and the chlorophyll behind its colour.
